Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 9:45am

Bukayo Saka scored a hat-trick in England's crazy win over France. (Getty Images: Luke Hales)

Bukayo Saka scored three goals to lead England to a 6-4 win over France for third place in the World Cup, while Kylian Mbappé surpassed Lionel Messi's career World Cup scoring record and took the lead in the Golden Boot race with a pair of second-half goals.

It was the highest-scoring World Cup game since Hungary beat El Salvador 10-1 in 1982, and the 10 goals were the most in a third-place match.

Saka had goals in the 37th minute and first-half stoppage time, then added his third on a penalty in the 87th for his second career hat-trick with England.

The Three Lions also got goals from Declan Rice and Ezri Konsa to build a 4-0 half-time lead and secure their best finish in a World Cup since winning their only title in 1966.

Jude Bellingham capped the scoring in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time, his seventh goal of the tournament.

Mbappé reached 22 career World Cup goals, one more than Messi. The star striker finished this World Cup with 10 goals, two ahead of Messi in the race for the Golden Boot, which is awarded to the tournament's top scorer.

Bradley Barcola and Ousmane Dembélé also scored for France.

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 9:45am

By Dean Bilton

I wasn't sure what to expect from this one, but you could have given me 100 guesses and I wouldn't have come up with that. A crazy game, one which I think will stick in the memory even with its low stakes.

But enough of that, because the real business is nearly upon us. This time tomorrow we will have a world champion, the World Cup final kicking off at 5am AEST on Monday. We will have heaps of build up this afternoon, the blog will be back bright and early tomorrow, we'll have colour and analysis and everything after the game. We have reached the finish line but we are not slowing down.

I hope you will join us for the big one tomorrow. Until then, thanks for your company today. Goodbye!

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 9:34am

By Dean Bilton

Mbappe scored his 22nd goal at World Cups today, which took him one clear of Lionel Messi in the all-time charts.

But it's not a record he's expecting to hold for too long.

"Messi is going to score tomorrow, that's for sure.

"I'm just trying to help my team win. When you score a lot of goals at the World Cup, it puts you in a certain category.

"I would have preferred not to be the all-time top scorer and to be playing tomorrow's match. It's good in terms of legacy, but today it's not the first thing on my mind."

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 9:30am

By Dean Bilton

This was Didier Deschamps's final game in charge of the French national team, a position he took up in 2012.

He led France to the World Cup title in 2018 and the final in 2022, as well as the final of the Euros in 2016.

Is that underperforming with such a talented group? Would be very harsh to say so. International football is decided by such fine margins, and he could so easily have a cabinet full of trophies for his time in charge. Still, that 2018 crown can never be taken away.

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 9:26am

By Dean Bilton

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 9:18am

By Dean Bilton

The bronze medals are being brought out on trays to be presented to the England players.

It's not what they wanted, but third does represent England's best finish at a World Cup since winning it in 1966. And that's not nothing.

Key Event

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 9:03am

By Dean Bilton

Where do you start? I genuinely have no idea.

England had 45 minutes of being totally dominant, 35 minutes of being totally hapless, and then another 20 or so of being competitive enough to see it out. If you add that all up, you get a 6-4 win. I think.

From 4-0 up at half-time, it did for a moment look like becoming one of the all-time English collapses, greater even than the all-time English collapse of just the other day. But the Three Lions got away with it in the end, steadied by the introduction of Jude Bellingham and the assistance of a late penalty.

France were diabolical in the first half and then briefly magical in the second. Mbappe and Olise decided they wanted a crack after the half-time break, and that was nearly enough to create something incredible. But there was too much to do, and they didn't deserve to win after what was offered up at the start.

Kylian Mbappe is now the World Cup's all-time greatest goalscorer (for now at least). Mbappe also leads the Golden Boot race by two (for now at least). Michael Olise has broken the record for most assists at a World Cup with seven. Bukayo Saka scored a hat-trick. Jude Bellingham finished with seven goals, the most of any English man at a World Cup. The ref got injured.

Crazy game. Head-spinning stuff.

Key Event

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 9:01am

By Dean Bilton

I'm sorry for the all-caps, but it's bloody 6-4 and Jude Bellingham has just run half the length of the pitch, dribbled back inside half the French defence and slotted one of the goals of the tournament.

He's a phenomenon. He has seven goals at this tournament, which is more than any Englishman has ever managed at a World Cup before.

Key Event

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:59am

By Dean Bilton

There's still time!

Turnover in midfield, Dembele is played through and this time finishes past Henderson. Pickford meanwhile is about 60 or 70 metres away from it over on the bench, which is simply not good enough really.

Probably a minute or two to play. Could they?

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:55am

By Dean Bilton

I think France have accepted their fate now. The same fate they looked to have accepted for the entire first half, in truth. But they certainly made a game of it for a while there.

Into stoppage time we go.

Key Event

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:50am

By Dean Bilton

It looks like they're going to get away with it. Those missed chances from Olise and Dembele have all added up, kept the door ajar, and Saka's penalty looks to have settled things for England.

It's a hat-trick for Saka, who has hardly been seen in this World Cup. Makes you think.

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:49am

By Dean Bilton

Djed Spence is too quick for Malo Gusto around the outside, and the England full-back is taken out by the tackle. It's a stonewall penalty and England will here have the chance to wrap this game up.

No Harry Kane though, so who takes it? Looks like it'll be Jude Bellingham.

Nope, at the last minute he gives it to Bukayo Saka who is on a hat-trick.

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:46am

By Dean Bilton

Just in case this absurd game couldn't get any weirder, the ref has stopped play so he can get a little calf massage.

And in that time, Jarell Quansah has gone down injured as well. He'll come off for Reece James, who given his history is probably only a few moments away from his own injury too.

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:45am

By Dean Bilton

The passing and moving between Mbappe, Olise and Dembele was brilliant, but that was a simple finish that Olise has sent wide. He simply had to score. The French forwards all hit the deck as one in disbelief.

Moments earlier, Bellingham broke through on goal to be one on one with the keeper but bizarrely opted not to shoot, and the chance passed him by.

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:44am

By Dean Bilton

Ivan Toney and Eberechi Eze are coming off for Elliot Anderson and Jude Bellingham. Tuchel trying to shore up the midfield, which has been porous in the second half.

Given his lack of regret at the tactical decisions made against Argentina, I'm surprised there's no Dan Burn.

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:40am

By Dean Bilton

There was a little tug on the jersey as he went down, but not enough to warrant a penalty in the referee's eyes.

Subsequently Digne has gone through Saka, who is limping away. Looks like Jude Bellingham will be introduced shortly.

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:38am

By Dean Bilton

Time stood still! Olise opened up his left foot to strike first time, and everyone was waiting for the net to ripple. The ball just faded wide of the post though, and England's lead remains for now.

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:33am

By Dean Bilton

The England defence has collapsed. Henderson is all over the shop in goal. Rice is totally out of gas in midfield. Mbappe and Olise are absolutely toying with them now.

Will this hydration break stop the French momentum? Because right now, they are looking unstoppable.

Spare a thought for Anthony Barry ...

Key Event

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:30am

By Dean Bilton

First thing's first, it's 4-3. Bonkers.

But that goal, Mbappe's second today, is his 22nd at World Cups. That takes him ahead of Lionel Messi and alone on top of the all-time charts.

It also puts him two goals clear of Messi in this year's Golden Boot race.

It's also Michael Olise's seventh assist of the tournament, which is a record.

This game is beyond insane.

Sun 19 Jul 2026 at 8:28am

By Dean Bilton

Geez, that's a real chance for France but such a tame effort from Dembele. Mbappe and Barcola set it up for Dembele, but he meekly rolls his effort straight at Henderson.

Still, the pressure comes. Henderson punts the ball straight into touch under no pressure and France come again through Upamecano, whose long-range strike is parried away.
